mainTopic: Whether the first and second סימנים join together to save an animal from נבלה impurity when the animal became a טרפה in the middle of the שחיטה, and a new teaching from ריש לקיש's rule about inviting people to eat the innards.
overview: The גמרא asks whether the two cuts of שחיטה still join together to save an animal from נבלה impurity when it became a טרפה between the first and second cut. It limits the question to טומאה only, since eating is surely forbidden. רב אחא בר רב then suggests רבי זירא never changed his view at all. Next, רב אחא בר יעקב learns from ריש לקיש that Jews may be invited to eat the innards of a convulsing slaughtered animal, but a גוי may not, because for a גוי only death permits the meat. A ברייתא disagrees: meat cut from the neck and eaten after the animal dies is permitted to both, and this supports רב אידי בר אבין. A new משנה teaches that if no blood came out during שחיטה, the meat was never made able to become טמא, while רבי שמעון says the שחיטה itself does this. The גמרא asks why impure hands, which are only a שני, would matter for חולין, and proves four ways that the משנה is about חולין. רב נחמן answers that the case is חולין bought with מעשר שני money, not following רבי מאיר. The משנה he quotes to show this comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Do the two cuts join to save the animal from נבלה impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the question clearly: does the first סימן join with the second סימן to keep the animal from becoming a נבלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the first סימן join with the second סימן to make the animal pure from the טומאה of a נבלה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out its question. The animal became a טרפה between the two cuts, so the two cuts were done for different purposes, and we ask whether they still count as one שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first cut was made while the animal was still fit, so it worked toward both permitting it for eating and keeping it pure. The second cut came after the animal became a טרפה, so it can only help with purity. The question is whether two cuts with different jobs can still add up to one valid שחיטה for purity.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the two organs cut in שחיטה (windpipe and food pipe)
an animal that died without a valid שחיטה; it is forbidden and carries טומאה

phrases.aramaic: מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: Does the first siman join with the second siman
phrases.notes: The first cut was made while the animal was still fit. The second came after it became a טרפה.

phrases.english: to purify it from the impurity of a carcass, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the dilemma that the earlier discussion of the סוגיא was leading up to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two cuts made for different purposes (one before and one after the animal became a טרפה) combine into one שחיטה to prevent נבלה impurity.

steps.title: The question is only about purity, not about eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the question to purity alone. Eating the animal is surely forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only asked about making it pure from the טומאה of a נבלה. But as for eating it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the limits of its own question. The doubt is only about טומאה, and everyone agrees the animal may not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating is forbidden for everyone, then everyone treats the animal as a טרפה. That would mean even רבי זירא accepts this, so he must have taken back his objection to רבא's distinction between the lungs and the innards. This conclusion is exactly what the next step questions.

keyTerms.meaning: we only had a question up to this point (that is, only about this case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two issues. Being forbidden to eat (טרפה) and carrying טומאה (נבלה) are separate questions. An animal can be a טרפה and still be saved from נבלה impurity by its שחיטה.

phrases.english: We only raised the question
about purifying it from the impurity of a carcass,
but as for eating, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dilemma of step 1 to purity alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animal is surely forbidden to eat. The doubt is only whether its שחיטה saves it from נבלה impurity. This implies רבי זירא retracted his objection.

steps.title: Maybe רבי זירא never changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב suggests that רבי זירא never retracted. He only argued from inside רבא's own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב said to רבינא: Perhaps רבי זירא really never took back his view. He was only speaking according to רבא's words, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר רב rejects the idea that רבי זירא took back his objection. He offers another way to read what רבי זירא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step assumed that רבי זירא first disagreed with רבא and later changed his mind. רב אחא בר רב says no: רבי זירא always held that a hole in either the lungs or the innards makes the animal a טרפה. His objection was only meant to show that רבא's distinction does not work on רבא's own terms.

keyTerms.meaning: he was arguing according to someone else's view
he does not hold that way himself

steps.whatToRemember: A sage sometimes argues 'according to your view' without agreeing with it. So you cannot always tell what a sage himself holds from the way he objects to someone else.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Rav said to Ravina:
Perhaps he actually did not retract,
and Rabbi Zeira was speaking according to Rava's words,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn in step 2 that רבי זירא retracted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that רבי זירא retracted his objection to רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumes that רבי זירא's objection showed his own view. But he may have been arguing only according to רבא, while always holding that the animal is a טרפה either way.

steps.title: From ריש לקיש: you may invite Jews to eat the innards, but not a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב draws a practical rule from ריש לקיש's teaching: Jews may be invited to eat the innards, but a גוי may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Learn from רבי שמעון בן לקיש that we may invite Jews to eat the innards, but we may not invite a גוי to eat the innards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to ריש לקיש's rule: once the windpipe is cut, the lung is treated as if it were already lying in a basket. רב אחא בר יעקב learns a practical הלכה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, it is the שחיטה that makes the animal permitted, so the innards may be eaten. For a גוי the innards are forbidden. The next step explains the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this (a conclusion drawn from an earlier statement)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ריש לקיש's rule is not just theory. It affects who is allowed to eat parts of the animal.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Learn from the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש's earlier rule: once the windpipe is cut, the lung is treated as if it were already in a basket.

phrases.english: that one may invite Jews to eat the innards,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין גּוֹי עַל בְּנֵי מֵעַיִין.
phrases.english: but one may not invite a gentile to eat the innards.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי זירא discussion and goes back to ריש לקיש's statement to learn a new practical rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jews may be invited to eat the innards of the slaughtered animal, but a גוי may not be invited to eat them.

steps.title: Why a Jew may eat the innards but a גוי may not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב אחא בר יעקב's rule. For a Jew, שחיטה permits the meat. For a גוי, only death permits it, so the innards of a still-living animal are like אבר מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? For a Jew, everything depends on שחיטה. Once there is a full, proper שחיטה, the meat is permitted to him. For גוים, stabbing the animal is enough and everything depends on the animal's death. So until it dies, these innards are like a limb from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule from Step 4 and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew's meat becomes permitted through the act of שחיטה, even while the animal still moves. A גוי does not need שחיטה at all. For him, the only thing that permits the meat is the animal's death, so before that moment the innards are forbidden as אבר מן החי.

keyTerms.meaning: Stabbing the animal, which is enough for a גוי
A limb taken from a living animal, forbidden even to a גוי

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גוי's meat needs more than the Jew's. A גוי needs less: no שחיטה at all. But because nothing except death permits his meat, he has to wait for the animal to die.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רב אחא בר יעקב split between a Jew and a גוי back in Step 4?

phrases.english: For a Jew, the matter depends on slaughter,
once there is a full, proper slaughter,
it is permitted to them;
gentiles, for whom stabbing is enough,
and for them the matter depends on death,
these innards are like a limb from a living animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the Jew/גוי rule stated in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are the innards permitted to a Jew but forbidden to a גוי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A Jew's meat depends on שחיטה. A גוי's meat depends on death, so before death the innards count as אבר מן החי.

steps.title: רב פפא almost asked a question but held back
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא wanted to ask רב אחא בר יעקב how anything could be permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי. He did not ask, because רב אחא had already given a reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: I was sitting in front of רב אחא בר יעקב and wanted to ask him: is there anything that is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי? But I did not ask, because I told myself: he gave a reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells about a challenge he thought of but decided not to raise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it sounds strange for a Jew to have a leniency that a גוי lacks. רב פפא held back because the reason in Step 5 explains it: the two are permitted in different ways, one through שחיטה and one through death.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything at all...? An opening for a challenge

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: I was sitting before Rav Acha bar Yaakov,
and I wanted to say to him:
Is there anything
that is permitted to a Jew but forbidden to gentiles?
But I did not say it to him,
because I said to myself: he did give a reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes a possible challenge to Step 4 that the reason in Step 5 already answers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew being allowed something a גוי is not is not a real problem here, because a reason was given.

steps.title: A ברייתא permits the meat to both Jew and גוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that meat cut from the neck of a slaughtered animal that is not yet dead is permitted to both a גוי and a Jew once the animal dies. This goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught, against רב אחא בר יעקב: Someone who wants to eat from an animal before it dies cuts an olive-sized piece of meat from the place of the שחיטה. He salts it very well, rinses it very well, waits until the animal dies, and eats it. Both a גוי and a Jew are permitted to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that disagrees with רב אחא בר יעקב's rule from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the meat is cut off while the animal is still alive, yet the ברייתא allows it even to a גוי. So the ברייתא does not treat such meat as אבר מן החי for a גוי. That goes against the split רב אחא בר יעקב made between Jew and גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with, against the view of
Before the animal dies, literally before its soul leaves
The place of slaughter, the neck
He salts it / he rinses it

steps.confusionAlert: He cuts the meat before death but eats it only after the animal dies. The question is whether meat separated while the animal was alive is forbidden to a גוי, and the ברייתא says it is not.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: It was taught, not in line with Rav Acha bar Yaakov:
One who wants to eat from an animal
before its soul leaves it,
cuts an olive's size of meat from the place of slaughter,
phrases.notes: This is after the שחיטה. He cuts from the neck while the animal is still moving.

phrases.english: and salts it very well,
and rinses it very well,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, וְאוֹכְלוֹ,
phrases.english: and waits for it until its soul leaves, and eats it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that goes against the rule explained in Steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's rule that a גוי may not eat innards from a convulsing slaughtered animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets a גוי eat meat that was cut off after שחיטה but before death. So such meat is not אבר מן החי for him, and there is no split between Jew and גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא shows that רב אחא בר יעקב's split between Jew and גוי is not accepted by this ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב אידי בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא supports רב אידי בר אבין, who said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן that someone who wants to get healthy may eat such meat, and that it is permitted to both a גוי and a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב אידי בר אבין. רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: Someone who wants to get healthy cuts an olive-sized piece of meat from the place of the animal's שחיטה. He salts it very well, rinses it very well, and waits until the animal dies. Both a גוי and a Jew are permitted to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא from Step 7 backs up an אמורא who taught the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי בר אבין's teaching matches the ברייתא almost word for word. He adds the purpose: eating this fresh meat helps a person get healthy. The key point is the same: there is no difference between a גוי and a Jew.
steps.whatToRemember: Meat cut from the neck after שחיטה, salted and rinsed well, can be eaten once the animal dies. Both the ברייתא and רב אידי בר אבין permit it to a Jew and a גוי alike, unlike רב אחא בר יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: This supports Rav Idi bar Avin,
for Rav Idi bar Avin said
that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan said:
One who wants to get healthy
cuts an olive's size of meat
from the place of the animal's slaughter,
and salts it very well,
and rinses it very well,
and waits for it until its soul leaves,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 7 as support for an אמורא who taught the same thing.
steps.raayaObject: רב אידי בר אבין's teaching, in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן, that such meat is permitted to both a Jew and a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in Step 7, which teaches the same procedure and the same result.

steps.title: Slaughter with no blood: the meat cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if no blood came out during שחיטה, the meat is kosher and may be eaten with impure hands, because blood never made it able to become טמא. רבי שמעון says the שחיטה itself makes it able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird, and no blood comes out, they are kosher. They may be eaten with impure hands, because blood never made them able to become impure. רבי שמעון says: the slaughter itself made them able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches a rule about meat that had no blood come out during שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it gets wet from one of the special liquids, and blood is one of them. With no blood, the meat was never made ready to become טמא, so impure hands cannot hurt it. רבי שמעון holds that the act of שחיטה is enough to make the meat ready to become טמא, even with no blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food able to become impure, usually through contact with a special liquid

steps.confusionAlert: 'כשרים' here means the meat is kosher to eat. 'הוכשרו' is a different idea: it means the food was made able to become טמא. The two words look alike but mean different things.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird
and blood did not come out of them: they are kosher,
and they may be eaten with impure hands,
because they were not made able to become impure by the blood.
phrases.notes: Food can only become impure after touching one of seven special liquids, and blood is one of them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: they were made able to become impure by the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף וְלֹא יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat from a שחיטה with no blood was not made able to become טמא and may be eaten with impure hands. רבי שמעון holds the שחיטה itself makes it able to become טמא.

steps.title: Why would impure hands matter even if blood came out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that if blood did come out, the meat may not be eaten with impure hands. It then asks why, since hands are only a שני and a שני cannot make חולין into a שלישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that no blood came out. So if blood did come out, it may not be eaten with impure hands. Why not? Hands are only second-degree impure, and a second-degree item cannot make non-sacred food third-degree impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden lesson out of the משנה and then challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that when blood came out, impure hands are a problem. But plain impure hands are only a שני לטומאה, and in חולין a שני cannot pass impurity on to make a שלישי. So even if the meat was made ready to become טמא, the hands should not be able to make it impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; used to point out what the rule depends on
But in the opposite case; used to draw an inference

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that blood did not come out of them,
but if blood did come out of them,
they may not be eaten with impure hands.
Why?
Hands are second-degree impure,
and a second-degree item does not make a third-degree in non-sacred food!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֹא יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם, הָא יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה in step 9 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule of the משנה that meat with blood may not be eaten with impure hands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hands are a שני, and a שני cannot make חולין into a שלישי, so impure hands should never be a problem for this meat.

steps.title: How do we know the משנה is about חולין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the משנה is about חולין. If it were about קדשים, a שני could make a שלישי, and the question would fall away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that we are dealing with non-sacred food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to back up its own question. It is setting up proofs that the משנה is about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from step 10 only works if the משנה is about חולין, because for קדשים a שני can make a שלישי. So the גמרא wants to rule out reading the משנה as talking about קדשים.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we are dealing with non-sacred food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the assumption behind the question in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the משנה is about חולין and not קדשים.

steps.title: First proof: the משנה lists a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions a חיה, a wild animal. Wild animals are never brought as קדשים, so the משנה must be about חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it teaches 'wild animal.' If it were about sacrifices, is there such a thing as a wild animal among sacrifices?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first proof that the משנה is about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only domestic animals and birds can be קרבנות; a חיה is never offered. Since the משנה includes a חיה in its list, it must be talking about ordinary meat.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild, undomesticated animal, such as a deer

phrases.english: Because it teaches 'wild animal,'
whereas if it were sacrifices,
is there such a thing as a wild animal among sacrifices?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a first proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about חולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's mention of חיה, which cannot be a קרבן.

steps.title: Second proof: a sacrifice with no blood would not be valid
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה were about קדשים, how could it call the animal כשר when no blood came out? A קרבן needs its blood for the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, if it is about sacrifices, when no blood comes out, is it valid? The sacrifice itself needs the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof that the משנה is about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן is only accepted when its blood is put on the מזבח. If no blood came out, the קרבן would be useless, so the משנה could not call it כשר. That makes sense only for ordinary meat.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is about sacrifices,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם – כְּשֵׁרָה?
phrases.english: when no blood comes out of them, is it valid?
It itself needs the blood!
phrases.notes: A sacrifice works through putting its blood on the altar, so with no blood there is nothing to bring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, אִי בְּקָדָשִׁים, כִּי לֹא יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to the one in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about חולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a קרבן requires its blood, so it cannot be כשר without blood.

steps.title: Third proof: sacrifice blood does not make food able to become impure
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה were about קדשים, blood coming out would not make the meat able to become טמא. רבי יוחנן learns from a פסוק that only blood poured like water, which means חולין blood, has that power.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, if it is about sacrifices, when blood comes out, does it make the meat able to become impure? But רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: How do we know that sacrifice blood does not make food able to become impure? Because it says: 'Upon the ground you shall pour it like water.' Blood that is poured like water makes food able to become impure. Blood that is not poured like water does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third proof, using a teaching of רבי יוחנן based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that blood coming out does make the meat ready to become טמא. Blood of חולין is poured on the ground like water, so it counts as a liquid for this. Blood of קדשים goes on the מזבח instead, so it does not, and the משנה must therefore be about חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes food able to become impure
You shall pour it like water

steps.whatToRemember: So far the גמרא has proved three ways that the משנה is about חולין: it lists a חיה, it calls a bloodless animal כשר, and it treats the blood as making the meat able to become טמא. The next step adds a fourth proof. Since the case is חולין, step 10's question still stands until step 16 answers it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the משנה is clearly about חולין, the גמרא cannot answer its question by saying the משנה is about קדשים. It will need a different answer.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is about sacrifices,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם מִי מַכְשִׁיר?
phrases.english: when blood comes out of them, does it make them able to become impure?
But didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that blood of sacrifices does not make food able to become impure?
As it is said: 'Upon the ground you shall pour it like water,'
blood that is poured like water makes food able to become impure,
blood that is not poured like water does not make food able to become impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, אִי בְּקָדָשִׁים, כִּי יָצָא מֵהֶן דָּם מִי מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third proof after steps 12 and 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about חולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching from 'על הארץ תשפכנו כמים' that sacrifice blood does not make food able to become impure.

steps.title: Holy food is already able to become impure without blood
steps.stepSummary: Another proof that the משנה is about חולין: if it were about קדשים, the meat could become טמא even with no blood, because חיבת הקודש makes holy food able to become טמא on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, if the משנה is about קדשים, why would they not be able to become impure when no blood came out? Let them become able to become impure because of the special regard for holiness, since we hold that regard for holiness makes holy food able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth proof that the משנה must be talking about חולין and not קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats blood coming out as what makes the meat able to become טמא. For holy food, that step is not needed, because חיבת הקודש already makes it able to become טמא. The משנה's focus on the blood only makes sense if the animal is חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: They become able to receive טומאה. This is the state called הכשר.
The special regard for holiness. Because of it, holy food can become טמא even without touching a liquid.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'able to become טמא' (הכשר) with actually becoming טמא. Here the question is only whether the food can receive טומאה at all.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is about sacrificial animals,
when no blood came out of them,
would they not be able to become impure?
Let them become able to become impure through regard for holiness!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling. Both mean 'let them become able.'

phrases.english: For we hold that regard for holiness makes them able to become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth proof, after steps 12, 13 and 14, that the משנה cannot be about קדשים.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about חולין, so step 10's question stands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted rule that חיבת הקודש makes holy food able to become טמא without contact with liquids.

steps.title: The case is ordinary food bought with second-tithe money
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, answers step 10's question. The משנה is about חולין bought with מעשר שני money, and it does not follow רבי מאיר. The גמרא begins to quote a משנה to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Here we are dealing with חולין that was bought with מעשר שני money, and this is not like רבי מאיר, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finally answers the question from step 10. The words 'as we learned' set up a משנה that the גמרא is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why impure hands, which are only a שני, would matter for חולין. רב נחמן answers that this חולין was bought with מעשר שני money. The food therefore takes on a stricter status, so a שני can affect it. He adds that this answer follows a view that disagrees with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with. It narrows the case.
Money used to redeem מעשר שני. Food bought with it in Jerusalem takes on מעשר status.
The second tithe, which is eaten in Jerusalem in purity.
And not according to. It shows whose opinion the answer does not follow.

steps.whatToRemember: The answer keeps the case as חולין, but chooses special חולין with a stricter status, bought with מעשר money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא saves a משנה by narrowing it to a specific case, even if that means it does not fit every תנא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Here, with non-sacred food that one bought
with tithe money, we are dealing,
phrases.notes: This means second-tithe money. Food bought with it takes on the tithe's status.

phrases.english: and not like Rabbi Meir, as we learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁלְּקָחָן בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 11 to 15 confirm the case is חולין, this step answers step 10's question by narrowing which חולין is meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ordinary חולין, where a שני cannot make a שלישי, so impure hands should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: חולין bought with מעשר שני money takes on a stricter status, so a שני can make it a שלישי. This follows a view that is not רבי מאיר's.
